title: In-yeast reconstruction of the African swine fever virus genome
author: Labroussaa, Mehinagic, et al.

steps.title: Concentrate ASFV particles and isolate DNA
steps.instruction: Concentrate viral particles from infected pig serum by ultracentrifugation and extract high‑molecular‑weight viral DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 mL of 20 % sucrose solution to a 13.2 mL ultra‑clear centrifuge tube (Beckman Coulter).
Overlay gently with 7 mL ASFV‑infected pig serum by pipetting down the tube wall.
Add PBS up to 2–3 mm from the top of the tube.
Centrifuge at 50,000 ×g for 90 min (follow rotor safety instructions).
Discard supernatant carefully; a pale‑white pellet should remain.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL PBS.
Extract viral DNA using the MagAttract HMW DNA Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Gel‑purify synthetic fragments 1 and 2
steps.instruction: Digest the synthetic plasmids, separate the linearized fragments on agarose, and recover purified DNA.

substeps.instruction: Digest 5 µg of pUC57‑Fragment1 plasmid in five 50 µL reactions (each containing 1 µg DNA) with SmaI following NEB instructions; repeat for pUC57‑Fragment2.
Load digested products on a 1 % TAE agarose gel containing RedSafe™ 1×.
Run electrophoresis for 1 h at 50 V (3.85 V/cm).
Excise the linearized DNA bands using an X‑tracta gel extractor after brief blue‑light illumination (avoid UV).
Elute DNA from the gel slice in 30 µL using the QIAQuick gel extraction kit (Qiagen).
Quantify DNA with a biospectrophotometer; use 100 fmol of each fragment for the subsequent transformation step.

steps.title: Linearize ASFV sub‑genomic fragments
steps.instruction: Digest each ASFV sub‑genomic fragment with I‑SceI to generate compatible ends for TAR cloning.

substeps.instruction: Digest 50 fmol of each sub‑genomic fragment with I‑SceI according to the enzyme’s manual; if DNA is limiting, set up multiple 50 µL reactions in parallel.
After 1 h incubation, add 1 µL I‑SceI to each reaction and incubate an additional hour.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA before yeast transformation
steps.instruction: Pool all digested fragments and precipitate them for efficient yeast spheroplast co‑transformation.

substeps.instruction: Combine all digested synthetic and TAR‑cloned fragments in a microcentrifuge tube.
Calculate the total volume (V_DNA) of the pooled fragments.
Add isopropanol (1/10 × V_DNA), 3 M sodium acetate (1/10 × V_DNA), 1 µL Glycoblue™ coprecipitant, and 1 µL tRNA.
Centrifuge at 12,500 ×g for 30 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 700 µL 70 % ethanol.
Centrifuge again at 12,500 ×g for 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 30 µL TE buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA).
Store at 4 °C if used immediately or at –20 °C for longer storage.

steps.title: Co‑transform yeast spheroplasts with fragments
steps.instruction: Introduce the pooled ASFV fragments together with the TAR vector into yeast spheroplasts.

substeps.instruction: Prepare yeast spheroplasts as described in the referenced step 14.
Mix the spheroplasts with 250 ng PCR‑amplified pCC1BAC‑His3 vector and the 30 µL pooled ASFV fragments.
Plate the transformation mixture on Sorbitol‑His plates (instead of Sorbitol‑Ura).
Incubate plates; transformants become visible after ~24 h and colonies are large enough to pick after ~48 h.

steps.title: Screen yeast transformants by multiplex PCR
steps.instruction: Verify the presence of all junctions between ASFV sub‑genomic fragments using two multiplex PCR assays.

substeps.instruction: Patch individual yeast colonies onto a fresh SD‑His plate.
Extract yeast genomic DNA using the GC‑prep method (step 17).
Set up two independent multiplex PCRs per colony with the Qiagen® Multiplex PCR Kit:
• 12.5 µL 2× Multiplex PCR Master Mix
• 2.5 µL 10× primer mix (2 µM each primer)
• 9 µL RNase‑free water
• 1 µL DNA template (GC‑prep)
• Total volume 25 µL
Run the following cycling program:
1) 95 °C 15 min (initial denaturation)
2) 95 °C 1 min (denaturation)
3) 50 °C 2.5 min (annealing)
4) 72 °C 1.5 min (extension)
Repeat steps 2–4 for 35 cycles
5) 68 °C 10 min (final extension)
6) Hold at 10 °C forever
Analyse PCR products on a 100 bp Plus DNA ladder (Thermo Scientific).
Select one or two colonies showing the expected band pattern as positive full‑length clones.
Biobank selected yeast clones at –80 °C in Roti®Store yeast cryo vials according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Large‑scale YAC DNA extraction from yeast
steps.instruction: Produce milligram‑scale quantities of the full‑length ASFV genome from yeast cultures.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 500 mL of S. cerevisiae containing the full‑length ASFV construct in SD‑His medium; grow at 30 °C with agitation in a 2 L baffled Erlenmeyer flask.
When OD₆₀₀ reaches ~2, harvest cells by centrifugation at 4,250 ×g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL P1 solution (Qiagen Large‑construct kit), 2 mL Zymolyase solution (per kit recipe), and 200 µL β‑mercaptoethanol.
Vortex 30 s and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Vortex another 30 s and incubate a second 1 h at 37 °C.
Extract the YAC DNA using the Qiagen® Large‑construct kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Plasmid DNA extraction from E. coli (optional)
steps.instruction: Obtain the ASFV construct from an E. coli host as an alternative to yeast extraction.

substeps.instruction: Repeat steps 20 and 21 (linearization and precipitation) using an S. cerevisiae clone that carries the full‑length ASFV construct.
Grow a 300 mL E. coli culture harboring the construct.
Extract plasmid DNA with the Qiagen® Large‑construct kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

Optional: Prepare agarose plugs containing intact ASFV chromosome‑sized DNA using the CHEF Bacterial Genomic DNA Plug Kit (Bio‑Rad 1703592) for yeast cultures or the CHEF Yeast Genomic DNA Plug Kit (Bio‑Rad 1703593) for yeast cultures.
